references.text: Direct source for Jesus' words. In Hosea 10:8, the prophet Hosea foretells Israel's judgment: "They will say to the mountains, 'Cover us!' and to the hills, 'Fall on us!'" Jesus quotes this prophecy and applies it to Jerusalem's coming destruction.

In Isaiah 2:19-21, it is described how people on the Lord's day will enter mountain clefts and rock crevices to hide from the terrifying majesty of the Lord—a related motif of seeking refuge in the mountains under God's judgment.

In Revelation 6:16, people cry out to the mountains and rocks: "Fall on us and hide us from the face of him who sits on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb!" This is a clear parallel that repeats the motif from Hosea 10:8 and Luke 23:30 in an end-times context.
In Revelation 9:6, it describes a time when people will seek death but not find it—a related theme of despair under God's judgment, where people would rather die than face what is coming.

In Isaiah 32:19, hail is spoken of falling upon the forest and the city laid in ruins—a judgment motif where nature is used as an instrument of God's punishment, parallel to the image of mountains falling upon people.

The immediate context in Luke 23:28-29, where Jesus speaks to the women of Jerusalem and warns of the coming judgment on the city, provides the background for the statement about the mountains and hills in verse 30.
